name: iso-ash-commands
checklist_item: L. Pokemon Trainer -- command statuses applied to ALLY_ALL and CONSUMED by a partner
description: Prove a Trainer command lands its status on EVERY ally (not just the caster) and that a surviving partner then CONSUMES it -- the partner-side recipe fires and the damage changes.
notes: The four commands and the ability that fires each, from the Beast Whistle (ARM_ORIG_STARTER_TRAINER_BEAST_WHISTLE): ONLY_RESISTDOWN_ATTACK (AWR) -> FOCUS FIRE -> STATUS_CHARGE_CF_FOCUS_FIRE; ONLY_EVADEUP_SPLASH_ATTACK (SPD) -> SPREAD OUT -> STATUS_EVASIVE_CF_SPREAD_OUT; ONLY_RESISTDOWN_AOE_ATTACK (TAL) -> AFFLICT -> STATUS_PROWESS_CF_AFFLICT; ONLY_ATTACKUP_SPLASH_ATTACK (LCK) -> FINISH IT -> STATUS_CONCENTRATION_CF_FINISH_IT. All four are Target: ALLY_ALL, so they land on the Trainer too -- 'the icon on EVERY affected ally, not only the caster' is the tell that separates a real group buff from a self-buff.

FOCUS FIRE is the one chosen here because its partner-side consumer (SKILL_CF_PARTNER_CMD_FOCUS_FIRE) needs BOTH the charge status on the partner AND STATUS_ARMORDOWN_00 on the target -- and the Trainer's own FOCUS FIRE applies that ARMORDOWN in the same proc. So one command sets up its own consumption and the whole loop is observable in one fight.

PARTNER SURVIVAL is the hard part of this scenario. The partner arrives from SKILL_CF_TRAINER_GRASS_1 at ON_COMBAT_START (WOLF_GRASS_08, HP 16), gated on HAS_ITEM ARM_ORIG_TRAINER_BALL_GRASS and cf_bond in [0,3). It must live long enough to take a hostile action while holding the charge, which is why the enemy here is a single low-ATK jelly rather than anything real.

KNOWN BLOCKER, from docs/research/test-checklist.md:1021-1023: the ball's Send Out abilities (CF_TRAINER_SUMMON_GRASS_T1_ATTACK ...) report usable=False and never appear in the combat action menu, cause unknown. This scenario therefore relies on the ON_COMBAT_START summon path, not on a manual send-out. If the partner does not appear, that blocker -- not this scenario -- is what to chase.
cf_bond IS persistent (Persistent: true on SKILL_CF_TRAINER_GOTTA_TRAIN_EM), so it IS readable as CF_COUNTER_cf_bond in state customData. It is the ONLY counter in the pack that is.

MEASURED 2026-08-26, three manifest bugs this file used to carry. (1) The partner's attack is JELLY_ACID_ATTACK, not MELEE_BASIC_ATTACK -- crucible_list_abilities on the live partner reports JELLY_ACID_ATTACK / ONLY_ARMORUP_OTHER_ATTACK / SHIELD_TAUNT_ATTACK / BASIC_MOVE / SKIP_TURN and nothing else, so s2 fired an ability the partner does not have and the consumer could never proc. (2) CF_COUNTER_cf_bond is NOT written at combat start. RecipeActionExecutor.ExecPersistCounter is the only writer and it runs on a COUNTER_ADD/SET proc, i.e. when SKILL_CF_TRAINER_GOTTA_TRAIN_EM fires ON_KILL. A Trainer that has never landed a kill has NO such key -- confirmed live: keys were exactly ['CF_TRAINER_LEVEL_SEEN','CF_TRAINER_STARTER']. The old bond_readable assert was therefore asserting a key that cannot exist yet; it was the MANIFEST that was wrong, not the counter. (3) The `enemy` evidence region is the upper-right enemy nameplate, which only renders while an enemy is hovered/targeted; captured cold it returns bare scenery. Enemy-side debuff visibility is now its own step (s1b) so it cannot silently sink the group-command verdict, which is a different claim.

(4) MEASURED 2026-08-26: a body created by crucible_combat_spawn has NO StatusEffectComponent, so it can neither carry nor report a status. Proven by running this scenario both ways in the same session: against the encounter's OWN rats, FOCUS FIRE stamped STATUS_ARMORDOWN_00 + STATUS_RESISTANCEDOWN_00 and both asserts passed; after wipe_enemies + spawn WOLF_GRASS_08, the identical proc left the spawned jelly at statuses=[] and crucible_combat_snapshot printed '(no StatusEffectComponent)' for it. CombatReader.ReadStatuses reports an absent component as [] (a real 'no statuses'), not null, so this does NOT show up as UNREADABLE -- it silently reads as a status that failed to land. THIS SCENARIO THEREFORE USES THE ENCOUNTER'S OWN ENEMIES: no wipe_enemies, no spawn. Never point a status assert at a spawned body.

fixture.notes:
REUSES THE batch-4class BED (built 2026-08-26 through real CHARACTER CREATION: Vampiric / Pacifist / Pokemon Trainer / Gary, confirmed on screen and by crucible_party_list). A dedicated bed was not built for this scenario: that party already satisfies this manifest's expect_classes and min_size, and README says extra party members do not invalidate an identity tell that names the subject. bench.py always loads a COPY, so sharing one backup across scenarios is safe as long as they run SERIALLY. Original build recipe for a dedicated bed is kept below.

ORIGINAL: BUILD RECIPE. New campaign -> CHARACTER CREATION for every slot. NEVER crucible_party_set_class: it rewrites ConfigName but not the display name, so the class is right in state and every screenshot shows a stale vanilla name -- that voided a whole verification run here. Save, copy the .ftk2 out of GameRuns\ into %USERPROFILE%\Backups\ftk2-fixtures under this name, then set status to 'built'. Slot 1 = Pokemon Trainer, carrying both ARM_ORIG_STARTER_TRAINER_BEAST_WHISTLE (equipped) and ARM_ORIG_TRAINER_BALL_GRASS. Keep CF_COUNTER_cf_bond under 3 so the stage-1 partner line is the one that fires.

setup.why: godmode ON tops HP up every tick and masks every HP effect.

Thin the encounter to ONE real monster. It must be a REAL one -- a crucible_combat_spawn body has no StatusEffectComponent and can never carry ARMORDOWN (see note 4) -- but all four of the encounter's monsters killed the HP-16 partner before its turn in 2 runs out of 3, and a dead partner cannot consume the command.

steps.label: the partner arrived at ON_COMBAT_START and is on the board

asserts.why: cf_bond is written ONLY by ExecPersistCounter on a GOTTA_TRAIN_EM (ON_KILL) proc, so a Trainer with no kill yet legitimately has no CF_COUNTER_cf_bond key. What this step CAN assert is that the Trainer's customData channel itself is readable -- a null customData would make every custom-feature assert in the pack blind.

tells.expect: the party HUD card reads "Pokemon Trainer" -- our class, not a vanilla one
a partner body on a PLAYER-side tile. Note the nickname feature: a partner called Sparky / Bubbles / Blaze is TrainerNicknamePatches working as designed, not a bug
a card for the partner in the ally/minion HUD

steps.label: Trainer fires FOCUS FIRE -- charge on EVERY ally, ARMORDOWN on the enemy

asserts.why: ALLY_ALL means the PARTNER too -- this assert is what separates a real group command from a self-buff

tells.expect: the party HUD card reads "Pokemon Trainer" -- our class, not a vanilla one

the Focus Fire marker icon above EVERY ONE of the four party cards (Vampiric, Pacifist, Pokemon Trainer, Gary) -- the same crop taken at s0 has no icons at all, so the icons are the proc. On the caster only is a FAIL for a group command
the same Focus Fire marker icon on the PARTNER's ally-minion card (Sparky) -- absent from the s0 capture of the same card, so the partner really was included in ALLY_ALL

steps.label: the enemy the Trainer marked shows its debuffs to the player

tells.expect: the party HUD card reads "Pokemon Trainer" -- our class, not a vanilla one

Armour Down / Resistance Down markers on the enemy the Trainer pointed at, on the board. NOTE the upper-right `enemy` nameplate region only renders while an enemy is hovered, so it is not usable for a cold capture

steps.label: hand the turn to the partner
the PARTNER attacks while charged -- SKILL_CF_PARTNER_CMD_FOCUS_FIRE consumes the command for +6 damage

asserts.why: the consumer adds a flat 6 on top of the partner's own hit, so the drop must be at least 6

tells.expect: the party HUD card reads "Pokemon Trainer" -- our class, not a vanilla one
the enemy the partner hit shows an HP drop clearly bigger than a plain partner hit -- its floating hp pill on the board

steps._ability_note: the partner's real hostile ability; MELEE_BASIC_ATTACK is not on its kit. SKILL_CF_PARTNER_CMD_FOCUS_FIRE gates on HOSTILE_ACTION=true plus ARMORDOWN on the trigger target, not on a particular ability id.

tells.expect: the party HUD card reads "Pokemon Trainer" -- our class, not a vanilla one
the Trainer and the partner are both still in the ally HUD
